findings: Entailment-oracle-relative lower validity uses safe back-off thresholds without universal nesting; tight upper bound has extra nesting condition.
Merger entailment equivalence does not assume statistical independence of claims.
Published finite order-statistic range is alpha>=1/(n+1).
Small author-annotated samples and repeated splits do not create new independent evidence; marginal validity excludes per-input and shifted guarantees.
Lower coherent-factuality bound can use actual subset truth without perfect proxy graphs; tight upper bound adds semantic graph and finite-threshold conditions.
Silver label shortcut relies on graph assumptions; direct gold subset labels are distinct.
FELM miscalibration, cyclic/long-output problems and subjective rubric limit generalization.
Regenerated outputs are a separately evaluated outcome, not automatically certified.
Registry/schema/result interface is a source-reported comparator for proposed integration; no local native execution.
Mature estimators and helpers have different reporting guarantees; optional backends add build costs.
Reported parity and selected coverage need exact harness/data/version reproduction.
Deterministic simulated replicas are not exact original-data replications; synthetic-control local optima differ.
Declared open-source package and commercial downstream product are distinct; rights need exact source review.
limitations: Author primary-text review, not independent review or empirical reproduction.
No new pixel review; six-image allowance exhausted. Pseudocode has alternate text extraction.
No downloaded code or live model executed. Underlying papers, repositories and model claims need separate originals before new technical reliance.
Public/authored benchmarks do not establish bank truth, identification, native capability, deployment prevalence or ROI.
Claim-dependency graph is not intervention DAG; inspection does not endorse every claim or close coverage.
